t: Fact Atomization Engine: a plain-language overview
title: Fact Atomization Engine: a plain-language overview
description: Overview: what the Fact Atomization Engine does and why archives need it. A fact atomization engine takes a long document and breaks it into its smallest true pieces — one claim per piece. 'The library opened in 1911 and holds 2 million books' becomes two separate facts. Each atom stands alone, can be checked alone, and can be retrieved alone.
provenance: Public methods compiled from standard information-extraction and knowledge-organization practice. Assembled for the JAH Databases archive.

t: How the Fact Atomization Engine works
title: How the Fact Atomization Engine works
description: Overview: what the Fact Atomization Engine does and why archives need it. Real atomizers segment text into sentences, then split compound sentences at clause boundaries (conjunctions, relative clauses, semicolons), producing candidate atomic claims. Each candidate passes atomicity checks: it must contain one verifiable proposition, its pronouns are flagged for coreference resolution ('it' → 'the library'), and temporal or spatial qualifiers stay attached to their claim. The output is a list of self-contained statements, each linked to its source sentence.
provenance: Public methods compiled from standard information-extraction and knowledge-organization practice. Assembled for the JAH Databases archive.

t: How the Fact Atomization Engine works: the deep tour
title: How the Fact Atomization Engine works: the deep tour
description: Overview: what the Fact Atomization Engine does and why archives need it. Real atomizers segment text into sentences, then split compound sentences at clause boundaries (conjunctions, relative clauses, semicolons), producing candidate atomic claims. Each candidate passes atomicity checks: it must contain one verifiable proposition, its pronouns are flagged for coreference resolution ('it' → 'the library'), and temporal or spatial qualifiers stay attached to their claim. The output is a list of self-contained statements, each linked to its source sentence. Advanced atomizers resolve pronouns before splitting so atoms stand truly alone, detect claims that span sentence boundaries, and score atomicity so borderline splits go to review. Quality is measured by claim-level precision (each atom is one true claim) and recall (no claim lost) against human-annotated splits. The limits are rhetorical and literary text where 'claims' are not really being made — the engine tags atoms by source genre so downstream checkers know what kind of truth they are verifying.
provenance: Public methods compiled from standard information-extraction and knowledge-organization practice. Assembled for the JAH Databases archive.
